detailed_rationale:
Prime Focus Ltd is a global post-production and visual-effects services provider (digital intermediate, VFX, 2D-to-3D conversion) operating across 18 cities on five continents. The business is genuinely cyclical at the industry level: the 2023 Hollywood strikes and subsequent streaming-spend pullback drove several years of weak demand, visible in a flat 0% three-year sales growth figure, before a clear recovery -- TTM sales growth of 30% and a return to profitability in the year to March 2026 (Rs 118 crore net profit on Rs 1,384 crore sales, 35% operating margin) after cycling through losses in 2024-25. The quant growth-divergence flag (3-year growth score far below the 1-year score) correctly captures this: the 'growth' being seen right now is a recovery off a depressed base, not new secular acceleration, and should be read that way rather than extrapolated forward at face value.

Leverage has also been rising through the downturn -- borrowings of about Rs 570 crore versus reserves that only recently turned positive (around Rs 200 crore) after being negative for a period -- and promoter holding has fallen materially, from 69.86% to 60.73% over the past year, a real dilution even as the business recovers. On the encouraging side, a subsidiary (PF Media Ltd) has just completed voluntary liquidation and the company exited a corporate insolvency process (CIRP closed by NCLAT, July 2026), suggesting legacy distress is being cleared up rather than papered over. Even so, three-year average ROE remains -14% despite a healthier 17% in the most recent year, underlining how volatile this earnings stream has been.

Reverse-DCF: at roughly 98x trailing earnings, the market is pricing a durable recovery in global VFX/post-production demand for several years running, on top of a company that was in insolvency proceedings as recently as this year and whose three-year average return on equity is still negative. Given the historical earnings volatility and the fact that the current growth reflects a bounce off a cyclical trough rather than a new structural driver, I judge this multiple too rich for the demonstrated durability of the recovery, and side with the quant Sell.
recommendation_rationale: The recent recovery (30% TTM sales growth, a return to profit) is real but is a bounce off a multi-year, strike-driven industry trough rather than new secular growth, and the stock trades at a rich ~98x trailing earnings for a business with a -14% three-year average ROE and legacy insolvency proceedings only just resolved. That combination of cyclical (not structural) growth and a demanding multiple keeps this at Sell.
summary: Prime Focus provides visual-effects and post-production services globally and is recovering well after a multi-year industry slump tied to the Hollywood strikes, returning to profit and posting strong recent revenue growth. However, that growth is a bounce back from a depressed base rather than new secular acceleration, the stock trades at a rich valuation for a business with volatile historical earnings, and a subsidiary only recently exited insolvency proceedings. We rate this a Sell given the price already assumes a durable recovery that has only just begun to show up in the numbers.
positive_para: The core VFX/post-production business has returned to solid profitability (Rs 118 crore net profit, 35% operating margin) with revenue accelerating 30% on a trailing basis as Hollywood production activity normalises, and the company has just cleared legacy distress by completing a subsidiary's liquidation and exiting insolvency proceedings -- both genuinely positive resolutions of past problems.
negative_para: The current growth is a recovery off a cyclical trough (three-year sales growth was flat at 0%) rather than new secular demand, three-year average ROE remains negative (-14%) despite the recent improvement, leverage has been rising through the downturn, and promoter holding has fallen from 69.9% to 60.7% in a year. At roughly 98x trailing earnings, the price already assumes this recovery is durable, which the company's volatile multi-year history and recent insolvency exposure do not yet support with confidence.
reverse_dcf_judgment: A ~98x P/E requires several more years of sustained global VFX/post-production demand recovery, but the current growth reflects a bounce off a depressed, strike-driven trough rather than a new structural driver, and three-year average ROE is still negative. Given the earnings volatility and only-just-resolved legacy distress, I judge the multiple rich relative to the durability actually demonstrated so far.
